_note: Local changelog rendered by whats-new.html. No network fetch — privacy-first. The full, canonical release history lives in changelog/*.md.

entries.title: The block succeeded. Now what?
changes: The block page is a decision, not a dashboard. It now shows why the page was interrupted, how much of the pause is left, and ONE thing you could make instead — with Show another, and Closest / Fastest / No cooking / Microwave filters. Three ways out, all on screen: go back, choose the alternative, or continue on purpose.

Continuing is now a scoped choice rather than an all-or-nothing switch: let this site through for your own site open time (5 minutes until you change it), 10 minutes, 30 minutes, or until you close the tab — or turn off all blocking for 30 minutes or until tomorrow. Every option is a scope plus a duration and says so — nothing offers a single-use pass, because declarativeNetRequest cannot report a single visit back and FitShield will not add a navigation listener to fake one. Passes carry absolute expiry timestamps, so they end correctly across a browser restart, a suspended worker, system sleep, and clock changes.

The alternatives catalog was rebuilt from 24 sketches into 88 entries you can actually cook: exact servings and quantities, temperatures, durations, and physical doneness cues, hands-on effort separate from elapsed time, equipment, allergens, realistic swaps, and storage notes. 46 full recipes and 42 quick fixes, covering pizza, burgers, fried chicken, tacos, burritos, rice bowls, noodles, pasta, sandwiches, breakfast, coffee-shop drinks, desserts, bakery cravings, late-night and convenience food, and Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Indian, Middle Eastern, Mediterranean, and Latin American cooking. 68 are vegetarian or stricter and 20 of those are vegan; 26 involve no heat at all and 37 need nothing hotter than a microwave — every craving has a vegetarian answer, and every craving that physically can be made without heat has a microwave-only one.

Suggestions are matched, not guessed. A deterministic local score uses the blocked brand’s own category and specialties, your diet and allergens (hard filters — you will never be shown something that breaks them), your pantry and equipment, how long you have, your favorites, and what you were shown recently. No AI, no network, no external recipe service.

Statistics now name only what FitShield can actually observe: ordering pages interrupted, times you left, times you continued, temporary passes used, and alternatives shown to you, chosen, and marked as made. Choosing an alternative is an intention; confirming you made it is a separate, optional step you take yourself. Your existing counts were carried over, not reset.

Categories now name what a brand actually sells. The block page and your statistics used to be handed an internal rule bucket, so every fast-food interruption was filed under "Fastfood" and every custom site under "Custom". Both now read the brand's real category — Pizza, Burger, Fast Casual, Coffee, Chicken, Tea and the rest. If you are upgrading, a one-time repair removes those two mislabeled rows from your most-blocked categories list; no interruption is forgotten, because the same events are still counted in your totals, your most-blocked sites, and your most-blocked countries. The old counts are not re-filed under the right categories — the real category was never recorded — so the list may look sparse at first and will fill in again as you use it. "Delivery" stays: it is a real category, not a bucket.

30 sites are no longer blocked, because they are not places you can order food from: fifteen same-city courier and errand platforms, the LINE messenger, a fitness app, four Jumia general storefronts, a discount store, and eight corporate and franchisor pages. Where one of those companies also runs a food service, the food service is still blocked — LINE MAN, Jumia Food and the rest were each checked. The curated catalog is now 2,505 brands across 111 markets, and the Courier category retired with them; if you were blocked at one before, it keeps its proper name in your statistics.

One brand, one switch. A brand's country sites had been split across the two blocklists, so the switches did not do what they said — turning "Fast food sites" off unblocked delivery platforms, and you could lose your local Wolt while keeping Wolt.com. 26 brands were affected; each now sits entirely under one switch. If you keep both switches on, nothing changes for you.

Settings asks about your schedule once. The simple start/end pair that sat alongside the window editor is gone — whichever of the two you edited second used to silently overwrite the first. Presets come first, with the full multi-window, per-weekday, overnight-capable editor behind a disclosure. The popup keeps a quick start/end pair, and disables it whenever your schedule is too detailed for two time inputs to represent honestly.

The first entry in the currency picker now reads "Match my language" followed by the currency and symbol it will use, instead of a globe emoji and a currency name that made the automatic option look like just another currency.

New: friction presets (light / standard / strict), a local weekly summary, kitchen preferences, your own custom alternatives, and a preview mode that shows exactly what an interruption looks like without recording anything or unblocking any site.
Repeat visits to a site you just continued to get one small, capped, explained addition to the pause — never an escalating lockout, and it can be switched off.
A local problem-reporting flow that shows you verbatim what it would say, strips paths and query strings down to a bare domain, and copies it to your clipboard. Nothing is transmitted by FitShield.

Settings backup now carries your kitchen, custom alternatives, schedules, friction profile, and favorites. Restore is size-limited, schema-checked, and validated in full before anything is written, and never restores an active pass.

entries.title: Play-ready, with complete app coverage
changes: Every tracked brand now has a researched, verified Android app status. All 1,280 remaining unconfirmed brands were checked against their official store listings — 243 new verified app mappings (now 1,545 packages covering 1,474 brands), 777 brands confirmed to have no official app, and 283 country storefronts of platform apps (Glovo, PedidosYa, Deliveroo, Wolt and friends) recorded on the brand that owns the app. Nothing is ever guessed.

Removed 10 corrupted blocklist entries the research exposed — including non-food sites that never belonged (a game publisher, a newspaper, a blood-donation service) and registry namespaces that could have over-blocked every site in an entire country domain space. FitShield should block precisely, and now it does.

The Android app is Play-Store-ready: this release builds the first signed bundle intended for upload, with the launch paperwork (release checklist, privacy and data-safety notes, store listing) finalized in the repository.

Under the hood, the project was reorganized into a clean engine / extension / android layout so contributors can find things — with shipped packages verified byte-for-byte identical in structure, so nothing changes for you.
Datasets bumped: fast-food v1.2 (2,111 entries), 2,575 blockable hosts generated for Android from the same canonical data the extension uses.

entries.title: FitShield goes native on Android
changes: FitShield is now a real Android app (preview): the same dashboard, stats, recipes, themes, and all 83 languages — reusing the exact web code the extension runs, so both platforms stay one product.

Blocks food-delivery and fast-food websites system-wide on Android with a local, on-device connection filter that works even with strict Private DNS (NextDNS) enabled. No traffic ever leaves your device to any FitShield server, DNS is untouched, and HTTPS is never decrypted.

Blocks food apps too: opt in, and opening a blocked app shows a FitShield pause screen with your stats, a matched recipe idea, a reflection timer, and an honest "open anyway" — 870+ verified app mappings generated from the same curated data, never guessed.
The block screens on both platforms now share the full experience: category-aware recipe suggestions, block reason, schedule status, and a localized "Learn more" link to fitshield.net.
The extension's block page now respects your system's reduced-motion setting, matching the rest of FitShield.

Android extras, all optional and off by default: "display over other apps" for a more reliable pause screen, an "extra reliability" background keep-alive, and battery-optimization guidance — each explained in plain language before you turn it on.

Groundwork for the Play Store: Android 15 target, release builds with no debug logging (no hostnames ever hit the log), and public privacy documentation of exactly what the app does — nothing collected, nothing transmitted.

entries.title: Deeper insights & a documented history
changes: Your Stats now shows your most blocked sites, categories, and countries — a private, on-device breakdown that updates as you go. Only aggregate counts of the brands you already block are kept; no URLs, pages, or browsing history are ever stored.

Backup is now "Export Data & Settings" / "Import Data & Settings" — one file already carries your settings, stats, dashboard layout, favorites, and preferences, now with versioned migration metadata so future restores stay reliable.

Expanded fast-food country coverage from 14 to 56 countries across major global brands (McDonald's, KFC, Burger King, Starbucks and more), added brand aliases for better matching, and validated every entry for clean codes and no duplicates.
Started a permanent changelog/ folder: every release now has its own notes, plus a living ROADMAP so the project's history and direction have a single source of truth.
Localized the new stats labels and food-category names, and kept every supported display language in sync.
Made the extension fully offline: the Settings support button is now rendered locally instead of loading a third-party image, so FitShield makes no network requests at all.

entries.title: Stats, Firefox & a wider dashboard
changes: Added a private, on-device Stats panel: blocked visits, estimated money saved, and calories avoided — with a configurable average meal cost and meal calories. No browsing history is ever stored.
Money saved now shows in your language's currency (₹, ¥, €, $ …), auto-picked from your language with country-aware default meal cost and calories — plus a manual currency override.
Backgrounds slowly shift their hue, and titles and the savings figure carry a gentle animated gradient (reduced-motion is respected).
On the block page, pick a suggested recipe with "I'll make this instead" to log the calories you avoided.
The block page now explains exactly why a site was blocked: the domain, rule type, food category, and countries.
FitShield now runs on Firefox and installs cleanly on Chromium browsers (Chrome, Brave, Edge) — a single source tree builds a clean package for each, with no 'background.scripts' manifest warning.
Added a proper FitShield extension icon.
Redesigned Settings to use wide screens better: cards reflow into columns and stack cleanly on narrow windows.
Added Reset options and confirmation dialogs (custom-site removal, resets, and a full factory reset), plus onboarding, local Backup & Restore, and the Chrome Web Store listing.
Added a living, layered background: soft color fields that drift on their own, vary subtly on each open, gain gentle parallax as you scroll, and respect reduced-motion.
Translated the new 0.51 screens (stats, reset, welcome tour, What's New, block reasons, recipe choices) across every supported language, and added German as a new display language.
Cleaned up the repository and consolidated branding assets into a Branding/ folder.

entries.title: Recipe suggestions & blocking fixes
changes: The block page now suggests a vegetarian and a meat/protein recipe based on what you blocked.
Fixed an international domain in the blocklist that was silently disabling all blocking.
Made the block screen reliably appear and show which brand triggered it.

entries.title: Localization
changes: Added 80+ display languages with a searchable language picker and a manual override.
Moved all interface text into the standard Chrome localization system.
